content.text:
All three bugs reproduce:
- `19.99` becomes `19.98` because `parseFloat("19.99") * 100` is `1998.9999…` and `Math.floor` truncates it.
- `-0.50` prints as `-1.-50` because `Math.floor` and `%` behave differently on negatives.
- `discount.js` uses `Math.floor` even though its comment says "rounded to the nearest cent".

I'll fix each one.

content.text:
Both customer symptoms are fixed: totals no longer lose a cent, and refund lines print as `-0.50` instead of `-1.-50`. `npm test` passes all 4 tests, including 3 new regression tests.

There were three bugs, in three files:

- **`parse.js`**: `toCents` used `Math.floor(parseFloat(price) * 100)`. Binary floating point makes `19.99 * 100` come out as `1998.9999…`, so flooring dropped a cent. It now uses `Math.round`.
- **`format.js`**: `formatCents` used `Math.floor` and `%` on the signed value. For `-50`, that gave `-1` and `-50`, printed as `-1.-50`. It now formats the absolute value and adds the sign once.
- **`discount.js`**: `discountCents` used `Math.floor`, though its comment says it rounds to the nearest cent. It now uses `Math.round`, which matches the comment. This is a behaviour change: a discount that was previously truncated can now be a cent larger. For example, 10% off 1.15 is now 12 cents instead of 11.

The new tests are in `test/invoice.test.js`. They cover `19.99` and `0.29 × 3`, refund lines of `-0.50` and `-19.99`, and a percent discount that rounds.

The repo is not under git, so I haven't committed anything.
